articles.title: Asa Tribe barred from England Lions tour under Ebola rules after Kenya trip
articles.summary: Glamorgan opener played for Jersey in Kenya last month. Entry ban brought in by St Kitts and Nevis government. The Glamorgan opener Asa Tribe has been barred from joining the England Lions tour of the Caribbean following a visit to Kenya and concerns over the recent outbreak of Ebola in east…
body: Tribe, 22, is able to represent his native Jersey until he wins a first senior England cap and played three List A games for the associate nation in Nairobi last month. From there he was due to join the England Lions squad in St Kitts and Nevis.

However, the emergence of the deadly Ebola virus in Kenya – with nine confirmed cases, including two fatalities – has seen the government of St Kitts and Nevis place an entry ban on recent non-national visitors to the country.

A spokesperson for the England and Wales Cricket Board said: “Asa Tribe was unable to enter Saint Kitts & Nevis, having recently travelled to Kenya. Saint Kitts & Nevis currently have a 21-day non-entry rule in place for non-nationals who have been in Kenya due to the Ebola situation in Kenya and seven other countries in Africa. Asa is back in the UK, and we are in touch with the relevant authorities.”

It is understood that after playing his final match in Nairobi on 27 October, Tribe was then intending to travel to St Kitts and Nevis using connecting flights. He had made it as far as Paris before discovering the problem.

articles.title: Wolff hails world champion Antonelli as role model in blast at F1’s ‘entitled moaners’
articles.summary: Mercedes team principal hits out at ‘selfish’ drivers. Antonelli says he will keep No 12 on his car next season. The Mercedes team principal, Toto Wolff, has described his Formula One world champion Kimi Antonelli as a new kind of racing driver who represents the future of the sport, comparing him…
body: Antonelli secured his first world championship in Mexico City on Sunday, completing an extraordinary achievement in becoming, at 20 years old, the youngest F1 champion in only his second season in the sport. The Italian’s attitude, enthusiasm and sense of fair play have been notable in what was a revelatory season for a driver so young and Wolff believed he had proved to be a gamechanger in more ways than one.

“This notion of win at all costs, selfish, opportunistic, ruthless for your own benefit, that model of racing driver has died. We have a new champion that represents values,” Wolff said. “Humility, integrity, loyalty, respect. Being himself. He should be a role model for many other young drivers.

“He should be a role model for the few entitled ones in Formula One. The endless moaners on the radio. The ones that complain, the ones that crash. Look at this kid of 20 years and then think what you can do in order to improve. That’s the message to these kids.”
Wolff did not name the targets of his ire but his comments will be lost on no one and clearly he believes Antonelli, who has been with Mercedes since he was 12, is an excellent role model.

articles.title: Australia omit star pace trio for England series
articles.summary: Australia's star pace trio of Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc will not feature in the upcoming white-ball series against England.
body: The veteran seamers played all three Tests in the recent 2-1 series defeat by South Africa and have been rested for the three-match ODI series that starts in Perth on 13 November.
Cummins and Hazlewood have also been left out for the five-match T20 series that begins on 21 November, while Starc, 36, has already retired from the format.
Fast bowler Mahli Beardman, 21, has been named in both squads and could make his international debut in ODIs, while uncapped wicketkeepers Sam Harper and Lachlan Shaw have been included for the T20s.
Alex Carey, Cooper Connolly, Cameron Green, Travis Head, Josh Inglis and Matt Renshaw, who also played in the South Africa series, are included for the ODIs but do not feature in the T20 squad.

articles.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
articles.summary: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at Palladium. For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world.
body: On Monday, Simon had boarded a Vueling flight from Bilbao for the Ballon d’Or ceremony. A World Cup winner, a tournament record breaker too – albeit one who that day in New Jersey said: “If my gloves could talk they would say they didn’t have to do much” – he knew there was a chance of winning the goalkeeper’s award. For a few weeks, he had wondered what he might say, ordering his thoughts as he drove into Lezama each morning as he had been doing virtually every day for 15 years. By the time he took to the Palladium stage, he knew. Delivered with a light in his eye and without notes, with a steady voice, the speech was 491 words long and lasted two minutes and 21 seconds.

To José Ángel Iribar, the legendary Athletic goalkeeper whose statue stands outside San Mamés and whose presence is felt everywhere inside, in whose honour they wear black. To Koldo Asua, the coach who told the boy arriving in Bilbao to leave his ego behind, that what truly matters is the human legacy you leave not the trophies you take: to be remembered as good people. To all those who, he said, had taught him to love a club, to the fans above all.

articles.title: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins to miss upcoming England matches
articles.summary: Starc and Hazlewood also rested before busy summer. Beardman and Shaw set to make their team debuts. Test captain Pat Cummins and fellow quicks Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood will be rested during Australia’s upcoming one-day and T20 series against England.
body: Australia will play three ODIs and five T20 internationals, but Cummins, Starc and Hazlewood were not named in either squad on Monday as the pace trio refresh for a gruelling 10 Tests in 14 weeks this summer.

Key batsmen Travis Head, Matthew Renshaw, Josh Inglis, Cooper Connolly and all-rounder Cameron Green will be managed through the T20 series following long tours to Zimbabwe and South Africa, as they prepare for four Tests against New Zealand and five in India.

“We are in the middle of a highly demanding phase of our schedule,” said chair of selectors, George Bailey. “Our multi-format players are transitioning directly from the tour of South Africa into an ODI and T20 series, leaving a narrow window to ensure the squad is physically prepared and fresh for the upcoming New Zealand Test series.

“Then, from when the Test players assemble in Perth through to the conclusion of the 150th anniversary Test against England, the team will have been on the road for more than 100 days. To manage this workload, each player’s build-up to the New Zealand series will be carefully planned and focused on individual’s physical and mental preparation.”

articles.title: Could former wonderkid Silva fulfil his potential at Dortmund?
articles.summary: While the Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was fluffing his lines at one end of the pitch, Fabio Silva was preparing to rewrite the script at the other. His late equaliser for Borussia Dortmund in Der Klassiker must be the most important goal of his career.
body: It was magnificent too. The first touch was perfection to protect the ball and give him just enough space to arrow a shot into the far corner with his second. An 89th-minute equaliser away to Bayern Munich to maintain Dortmund's unbeaten record.

There is a feeling within Dortmund that he needed this as a reward for his efforts. Speaking to goalkeeper Gregor Kobel afterwards, he made the point that forwards need goals to feel good. Stealing the show from Kane could be a transformative moment.

Silva's potential has long been debated. He was just 18 when Wolves committed £30m to sign him from Porto, the club's chairman talking of a generational talent. Nominated for the Golden Boy award, this was the very definition of the precocious wonderkid.

But thrust into Premier League action before he was ready proved a struggle. Sixty-two appearances in the competition yielded only four goals, with mixed fortunes on loan at Anderlecht, PSV and Rangers before more promising signs at Las Palmas in LaLiga.

articles.title: Boulter wins in Hong Kong after incident 'got under my skin'
articles.summary: Katie Boulter battled into the second round of the Hong Kong Open with a straight-sets victory over Viktorija Golubic, despite an incident that "got under my skin", according to the British No 1.
body: Boulter was twice broken when serving for the match in the second set, having complained to the umpire when up 5-2 after a point was not replayed despite her being distracted by a noise from outside the court.

She ultimately triumphed in a tiebreak to take the match 6-2 7-6 (7-2), clinching a fourth win in five following on from reaching the semi-finals in Japan Open last month that saw her reclaim top spot from Sonay Kartal as British No 1.
Boulter, ranked 49th in the world and seeded eighth at the tournament, had got the better of Golubic in Osaka two weeks ago and repeated the feat in her Hong Kong opener.
She was broken early on by the Swiss but hit back to win eight games in a row to take the first set and control the second.

articles.title: Ravens reportedly interested in trading for veteran quarterback
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens’ season took a devastating turn on Sunday, when star quarterback Lamar Jackson injured his throwing thumb on the first play of a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Now, with backup Tyler Huntley also banged up, the Ravens could reportedly turn to the trade market for help.
body: According to one report, the Ravens could be targeting a veteran quarterback to help shore up the position, but it sounds like they’ll have to be ready to spend.

Jackson, who had just returned from a three-game absence due to an ankle injury, was hurt when his right hand struck Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau on a throw. He headed to the locker room and later returned to the sideline with his hand in a cast.

After the game, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed that Jackson will undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve. Asked whether the injury could end Jackson’s season, Minter said, “potentially.”
“It’s tough,” Minter said. “When it happened, I think at the time, you’re just hoping that maybe it’s something small, and then I think pretty quickly kind of realized what had happened.”
